body.statement:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), there are \(c,C>0\) such that \[\inf_{\widetilde
u_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_n^{
u}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde
u_n,
u_P)]\ge rac{c}{\sqrt n}\] and, uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), \[\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)Vert_1]\ge c\min\left\{1, rac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}ight\}.\] Each inequality is certified by an explicit two-point path inside the displayed Bernoulli proxy factorization. The quotient-law path has one-observation Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C/n\) and \(W_1\)-separation at least \(c/\sqrt n\). For the labeled path, a weight displacement \(h\) preserves both proxy conditional-independence factorizations, positivity, and rank, has one-observation observed-data Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(C g^2h^2\), and has ordered-weight separation at least \(c|h|\); taking \(|h|=c\min\{1,(\sqrt n g)^{-1}\}\) gives the second bound.
body.proof_tex:
We use explicit two-point reductions in the finite Bernoulli experiment.  For the quotient law, compare \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) with \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\).  The observed vector \((T,X_2,Z_2,Y)\) has finite support.  At \(\varepsilon=0\), every cell in the common support has mass bounded below by a positive numerical constant, and each cell mass is affine in \(\varepsilon\).  If the two mass functions are \(q_\varepsilon,q_0\), then \(\log x\le x-1\) gives
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q_\varepsilon\Vert q_0)
\le\sum_x\frac{\{q_\varepsilon(x)-q_0(x)\}^2}{q_0(x)}
\le C_1\varepsilon^2.                                                         \tag{66}
\]
Choose \(0<a\le1/8\) with \(C_1a^2\le c_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  The witness proposition puts both laws in \(\mathcal M\), and (66) puts them in \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\).  Their target separation is
\[
W_1\!\left(\delta_{0.25},0.4\delta_{0.25-a/\sqrt n}
+0.6\delta_{0.25+a/\sqrt n}\right)=\frac a{\sqrt n}.                        \tag{67}
\]

For the labeled experiment, define
\[
b_1(h):=0.2,\qquad b_2(h):=\frac{0.48-0.2h}{0.6-h},\qquad
B_h:=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\b_1(h)&b_2(h)\end{pmatrix}.                         \tag{68}
\]
Let \((q_0,s_0)=(0.48,0.24)\), \((q_1,s_1)=(0.52,0.32)\), and set
\[
w_t(h)^\top:=(q_t,s_t)(B_h^\top)^{-1}.                                       \tag{69}
\]
At \(h=0\), these are \(w_0(0)=(0.24,0.24)^\top\) and \(w_1(0)=(0.16,0.36)^\top\).  Put
\[
J_t:=A_t\operatorname{diag}(w_t(0))B_0^\top,qquad
A_{t,h}:=J_t(B_h^\top)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))^{-1}.                 \tag{70}
\]
The first row of \(A_{t,h}\) is \((1,1)\), since the first row of \(J_t\) is \((q_t,s_t)=w_t(h)^\top B_h^\top\), and
\[
A_{t,h}\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))B_h^\top=J_t.                              \tag{71}
\]
For binary \((X_2,Z_2)\), the entries of \(J_t\) determine all armwise probabilities of \((T,X_2,Z_2)\), so (71) keeps that observed margin fixed.  Summing (69) over \(t\) and using
\[
(1,0.56)=(0.4+h,0.6-h)B_h^\top
\]
shows that the new latent masses are \((0.4+h,0.6-h)\).  Define
\[
P(T=1\mid U=u)=\frac{w_{1u}(h)}{p_u(h)},\qquad
\mu_0=(0.25,0.25),\qquad
\mu_1=(0.5-g/2,0.5+g/2),                                                      \tag{72}
\]
and generate the Bernoulli variables with the witness's conditional-independence factorization; call the resulting law \(P_{g,h}\).

All quantities in (68)--(70) are rational and continuous near zero.  At zero, all Bernoulli probabilities and joint weights have strict interior slack, and the witness has strict rank slack.  Hence a numerical \(h_0>0\) exists such that, for \(|h|\le h_0\), every probability lies in \((0,1)\), every joint latent--arm mass exceeds \(0.1\), and every relevant smallest singular value exceeds \(0.1\).  These bounds are uniform in \(g\in[0,1/4]\), because the proxy and treatment quantities do not depend on \(g\).  Bernoulli support gives the retained observable envelopes with \(L=2\), and the construction gives the two proxy separations, consistency, and armwise ignorability.  The effects in (72) are \(0.25-g/2\) and \(0.25+g/2\), with gap exactly \(g\).  Therefore
\[
P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g),\qquad |h|\le h_0,\quad 0<g\le1/4.                  \tag{73}
\]
For \(t=0\), the outcome success probability is the common \(0.25\), so (71) makes the entire observed arm-zero law independent of \(h\).  For \(t=1\), every observed cell probability has the form
\[
q_{g,h}(t,x,z,y)=\frac12q_h(t,x,z)+(2y-1)\frac g2H_{t,x,z}(h),                \tag{74}
\]
where \(q_h(t,x,z)\) is independent of \(h\) by (71), and \(H_{t,x,z}\) is a smooth finite sum of the weights and Bernoulli proxy probabilities above.  On \(|h|\le h_0\), the mean-value theorem gives
\[
|q_{g,h}(x)-q_{g,0}(x)|\le C_2g|h|.                                          \tag{75}
\]
All cells under \(P_{g,0}=P_{g/2}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) are continuous and strictly positive for \(g\in[0,1/4]\); compactness of that interval gives a uniform lower bound.  The chi-square calculation in (66) then yields
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}((P_{g,h})_O\Vert(P_{g,0})_O)\le C_3g^2h^2.                  \tag{76}
\]
Effects remain ordered, and so
\[
\lVert p^\uparrow(P_{g,h})-p^\uparrow(P_{g,0})\rVert_1=2|h|.                \tag{77}
\]
Take \(|h|=a\min\{1,(\sqrt n g)^{-1}\}\), with \(a\le h_0\) and \(C_3a^2\le c_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  Then (73)--(76) put both points in \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\), and (77) is the asserted separation.

Finally, for two laws \(Q_0,Q_1\) whose targets are separated by \(\Delta\), integration of the triangle inequality against the smaller of their two densities gives
\[
\max_iE_{Q_i}\ell(\widehat\theta,\theta_i)
\ge\frac\Delta2\{1-\lVert Q_0-Q_1\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}.                   \tag{78}
\]
Applying the log-sum inequality to a set attaining total variation and the elementary binary relative-entropy bound gives
\[
\lVert Q_0-Q_1\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_1\Vert Q_0)/2}.                                  \tag{79}
\]
Kullback--Leibler divergence of product laws is \(n\) times the one-observation divergence.  Decrease \(a\) so that (79) makes the braces in (78) at least one half.  Substitution of (67) and (77) proves both lower bounds with constants uniform in the displayed regimes.
body.justification: The verified factorization-preserving paths distinguish quotient-law regularity from labeled-coordinate irregularity in the actual observed proxy experiment.
body.gap: Ordinary-mixture collision lower bounds do not preserve the VMW proxy factorization and therefore do not establish the observed-data Kullback--Leibler order required here.
body.consumer: The converse calibrates both the smallest possible law-level radius and the separation needed for defensible labeled-weight reporting.
